Analyzing opentofu-bin AUR package with openrouter/free
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard PKGBUILD for the `opentofu-bin` package, which distributes prebuilt OpenTofu binaries. The source array downloads official release zips directly from `https://github.com/opentofu/opentofu/releases/download/...`, which is the project's legitimate upstream GitHub releases location.

The top-level scope contains only variable assignments (pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, arch, license, sources, checksums) with standard parameter expansion (`${pkgver//_/-}`). There is no `pkgver()` function and no obfuscated code, no `eval`, no `curl|bash`-style patterns, no unexpected network calls, and no top-level command substitutions that would execute external code during sourcing.

Notably, all architecture-specific SHA256 checksums are explicitly pinned (not SKIP), which is good hygiene. The `package()` function contains only a simple `install` invocation, but it is irrelevant to this gate since `--nobuild`/`--noprepare` prevent it from running.

Running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will only fetch the upstream release archives and parse/sourcing the PKGBUILD, all of which is benign.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard opentofu-bin PKGBUILD; only fetches pinned upstream GitHub releases.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a legitimate package for OpenTofu, an open infrastructure as code tool. The file downloads prebuilt binaries from the official GitHub releases of the opentofu project (github.com/opentofu/opentofu), which is the expected upstream source. Each architecture has a corresponding source URL and sha256sum checksum, all of which are properly provided (not SKIP). The package() function simply installs the bundled `tofu` binary to `$pkgdir/usr/bin/tofu` using standard Arch packaging conventions (`install -m 755`). There are no network requests beyond the initial source download, no obfuscated code, no use of eval/base64/curl/wget in the build script, and no system modifications beyond placing the binary in the expected location. The code is consistent with ordinary AUR packaging practices for binary distributions.
</details>

That code is also ordinary packaging behavior: installing the `tofu` binary into `$pkgdir/usr/bin/tofu`. No suspicious network destinations, obfuscated code, or dangerous runtime behavior is present. </details>
